text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has based its monetary programme for next year on an assumption of a five percent increase in gross national product (GDP) and an inflation rate of between 4.9 percent to 5.8 percent.
- The European Parliament is concerned over the expulsion of Frantisek Gaulieder from parliament and calls on the body to consider his reinstatement.
- The government has denied reports carried by private radio Twist that the EU will, without further warning, cancel Slovakia's association agreement if it fails to fulfill democratic principles.

SME - Slovakia's Roman Catholic Primate Cardinal Korec and the Bishops Conference have condemned recent anonymous threats against Milan Cic, chairman of the constitutional court and expressed their full support for Cic.
- Slovakia's parliament in January is to decide whether to call a referendum on NATO membership.
- The recent attack against Bratislava rabbi Baruch Myers was an assault against Slovak culture.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Oil and gas storage company Nafta is expanding its activities abroad to include Vietnam and Kazakhstan.
- More than 18,000 workers at steelmaker VSZ have decide to join the new independent Metalurg trade union and resign from the Kovo trade union, which is a memebr of the confederation of trade unions.
SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - The vast majority of young drug addicts lives in Bratislava.
- There was no debate on the state of the country address by President Michal Kovac to parliament, as the report contained nothing new.

- The parliamentary opposition has lodged a motion with the Constitutional Court asking it to review the legitimacy of the mandate of Jan Beran who was co-opted to parliament in place of Frantisek Gaulieder.
PRACA - Public opinion is almost equally divided over whether Slovak and foreign media present a true or false image of Slovakia, according to a recent poll.
